title: YOLOv12 benchmark and evaluation
stop_authority: Sprint 21 §3 — 'If YOLOv12 cannot legally be integrated under the current policy: STOP the integration and report the blocker.'
summary: The official YOLOv12 implementation is AGPL-3.0 and is a fork of Ultralytics that installs as the 'ultralytics' package. The model is the framework, so unlike a dependency it cannot be swapped out. ADR-0003 already blocks yolov8 and yolo11 on this licence; YOLOv12 is the same blocker with one fewer escape route. No YOLOv12 code entered the repository and no benchmark was produced.

source.paper: Tian, Ye & Doermann — YOLOv12: Attention-Centric Real-Time Object Detectors, arXiv:2502.12524 (2025-02-19)

findings.note: published from the same repository under the same terms

license_analysis.reason: Guardian ships a commercial product; AGPL-3.0 §13 reaches a deployed service. The usual mitigation of keeping the model and replacing the framework does not apply because the implementation is Ultralytics itself.

detector_family.change: registered in the reserved table with its reason; previously failed as a generic 'unknown detector family'

edge_license_policy.behaviour: refuses an AGPL manifest at model load (ADR-0009)

not_performed.promotion_gate: not run — the gate compares two evaluated models and there is only one
not_performed.reason: Measuring a model that cannot ship spends GPU budget on a number that changes no decision, and would leave AGPL code in the tree while doing it.

guardian_v1_baseline.source: Sprint 20.2 measurements, not re-run for this sprint
caveats: Precision and recall describe four rooms, not generalization: every validation scene is also a training scene (candidate provenance review). The scene-leakage defect is fixed for future imports; this published version predates it and is immutable.
Latency is development hardware. The 111.462 ms allowance is a Colab CPU figure and 35.51 ms is Apple M4 Max. Neither is a Jetson.

promotion_eligibility.basis: licence, not measured merit — it cannot be exported, loaded or shipped under ADR-0003

unblocking_paths.requires: an ADR — it changes ADR-0003's premise

unblocking_paths.note: Architectures are not themselves copyrightable, so a clean-room implementation is legally plausible. Sprint 19 already tried writing Guardian's own detector: the audit found it could not converge objectness on a single overfit example while the official implementation converged cleanly on the same one. That is measured evidence, in this repository, that this path costs more than it looks like.
AGPL §13 reaches a deployed service and Guardian ships commercially to kindergartens. ADR-0003 decided this.

recommendation.primary: Do not integrate YOLOv12 under the current policy. Close Sprint 21 at the blocker.
recommendation.if_pursuing_accuracy: Evaluate RT-DETR instead — already reserved in the family table as Apache-2.0 and scheduled after YOLOX. It answers the same underlying question ('is there a better detector than YOLOX-tiny') with no licence purchase and no blocker. It costs a sprint rather than a contract.
recommendation.ordering: The YOLOv12 decision is commercial before it is technical. Price the enterprise licence first; benchmarking after a licence is a defensible experiment, integrating first and resolving the licence later is not.

limitations: Licence texts were read from main on 2026-08-15; licences change and a re-audit should precede any future attempt.
This is an engineering reading of published licence files, not legal advice.
No claim is made about YOLOv12's technical merit. It may well be better than YOLOX-tiny; this sprint does not know, and nothing here should be cited as evidence either way.
The audit covered the official implementation and its upstream. A permissively-licensed third-party implementation could exist and was not found.
